title: dedicated-autoscaler-priority-burst-throughput-guarantees-and-util-reporting-enhancement
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: customers on Dedicated asked for stronger throughput guarantees for high-priority routes while still allowing controlled bursts for best-effort workloads. This PR implements priority-aware burst controls, token-bucket smoothing for throughput guarantees, and adds richer utilization reporting to the fleet telemetry pipeline. The goals are: 1) provide per-priority throughput SLOs that autoscaler can honor during contention, 2) reduce latency spikes caused by unbounded burst draining, and 3) surface per-fleet and per-priority utilization metrics to the Console for capacity planning.

What this changes: - Autoscaler: add 'priority_rules' to the DedicatedAutoscaler config schema (max_instances_per_priority, min_throughput_tps, burst_tokens, smoothing_window_ms). The autoscaler now enforces throughput guarantees using a token-bucket with smoothing to prevent short over-provisioning spikes. - Scheduler: priority-aware queueing + fair-drain when capacity is constrained. High-priority routes get reserved token allowance; low-priority can consume leftover burst tokens. - Metrics: new Prometheus metrics (dedicated_autoscaler_assigned_tps, dedicated_autoscaler_burst_tokens, dedicated_fleet_utilization_by_priority) with labels {fleet,region,priority}. Instrumentation added to autoscaler and runtime adapters. - Reporting: pipeline updates in observability-pack to aggregate per-fleet hourly utilization, 95/99 percentiles for burst consumption, and rollback signals for sustained over-bursting. - Tests: add unit and integration tests for token-bucket behavior and a canary e2e that simulates mixed-priority traffic. - Ops: feature-flag rollout (ff.autoscaler.priority_burst) and a canary runbook added.

Backward compatibility: new config fields are optional; behavior is gated behind ff.autoscaler.priority_burst until the end of canary. Existing clusters continue to use current autoscaler behavior if fields are absent.

Rollout plan: - Enable ff for 5% of fleets (nightly) - Observe metrics for 24h - Increase to 25% with additional canary traffic patterns - Full rollout only after 7 days with performance SLOs met.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-9142)
- [x] Schema migration with defaults
- [x] Unit & integration tests
- [x] Prom metrics + dashboards
- [x] Canary runbook + feature flag

Notes: integration tests were flaky on first run due to timing in the token refill logic; fixed by increasing clock tolerance in test harness and re-running CI.

review_comments: Evan Zhang: Nice, this addresses the core issue we saw during the Q4 incident. A couple of asks: 1) can we make min_throughput_tps configurable per-tenant later? 2) Please add an alternate path for fleets without metrics ingestion (we can't assume Prom always available).

Priya Nair (author): Thanks Evan — answered inline: 1) added TODO in schema and created ENG-9260 to track per-tenant override work; 2) autoscaler falls back to local counters when Prom is unavailable, documented in docs/design/dedicated-autoscaler-priority-burst.md

Miguel Torres: Tests look good. Integration e2e had a timing flake; suggest using the test harness virtual clock (we did that in second commit). Also add a note about SLO regressions in the rollout plan.
Priya Nair (author): Added clock tolerance and clarified SLO rollback conditions in the runbook.
merge_summary: Squashed 7 commits into main. Verified canary for 48h across 3 regions; metrics show stable p95 latency and no sustained over-bursting. Docs and dashboards shipped.
release_notes: Enhancement: Priority-aware burst controls and throughput guarantees for Dedicated autoscaler. Adds optional priority_rules to autoscaler config, new per-priority utilization metrics, and observability dashboards. Feature gated behind ff.autoscaler.priority_burst.
canary_runbook_summary: Enable feature flag for 5% fleets -> monitor dedicated_fleet_utilization_by_priority, dedicated_autoscaler_burst_tokens, p95 latency -> if burst tokens consumed > 80% for > 1h rollback flag and open INC ticket
notes: Follow-up: ENG-9260 to add per-tenant overrides; SUP-778 linked for customer support investigation.
